articles.title: Barragem Arroio São Luiz: Moradores de São Marcos podem voltar para casa | G1
articles.standfirst: Obras necessárias na estrutura e mudança do estado de emergência para o de alerta fizeram com que autoridades liberassem a volta dos moradores à região em São Marcos, cidade da Serra Gaúcha.
articles.summary: Após o afastamento do risco de rompimento na Barragem Arroio São Luiz, a Corsan e a prefeitura de São Marcos autorizaram o retorno de 170 moradores às suas casas.
articles.body:
Foram mais de 72 horas fora de casa. Agora, neste domingo (27), mais de 170 pessoas que tiveram de deixar suas moradias em São Marcos , em razão do risco de a Barragem Arroio São Luiz romper, têm autorização para retornar ao imóvel.

O prefeito de São Marcos, Volmir Rech, comunicou a decisão:

"Saímos do estado de emergência para o de alerta com relação à nossa barragem. Temos de agradecer à força de trabalho para nos ajudar nesse momento tão difícil. A normalidade vai voltar, conseguimos manter o abastecimento e continuamos com algumas ações."

"Fizemos o rebaixamento do nível da barragem para margem de segurança, tamponamento das fissuras e avaliação técnica. Lembrando que iniciamos o estado de emergência de forma preventiva, para garantir a segurança das pessoas. Continuamos em obras", complementou a diretora de operações da Corsan Aegea, concessionária responsável pela barragem.

Entenda como foi a retirada de moradores

A Defesa Civil do Rio Grande do Sul emitiu um alerta de perigo muito alto para a chance de colapso iminente da Barragem Arroio São Luiz , em São Marcos, município de 21 mil habitantes a 170 km de Porto Alegre, na quarta-feira (23).

"Estejam atentos às orientações dos órgãos de emergência e preparados para evacuação. Procure informações junto à Defesa Civil da sua cidade, conheça os Planos de Contingência municipais para saber quais os riscos e como agir em caso de desastre no seu município", afirma o alerta. (Veja nota abaixo)

A Corsan Aegea, responsável pela gestão do local, informou que "identificou trinca com vazamento na estrutura do vertedouro e em partes do contraforte da barragem" , que "o alerta está restrito aos imóveis localizados próximos à estrutura e às margens do Rio Jaguari" e que "as demais áreas da cidade não estão sob risco". (Leia nota abaixo)

⚠️ Um mapa aponta aponta a área de risco de potencial alagamento em caso de rompimento da barragem. A simulação descreve a área que poderia ser atingida, o sentido de fluxo de água e as residências que estariam sob risco. (Veja abaixo)

Como medida preventiva, aproximadamente 170 pessoas que vivem na área de alerta estão sendo retiradas temporariamente . As famílias estão sendo deslocadas para locais seguros até a conclusão da avaliação técnica já contratada pela companhia. O laudo dos especialistas permitirá dimensionar a situação e indicar as condições para o retorno aos imóveis.

Segundo a companhia, houve precipitação de 174 milímetros em 24 horas na cidade — conforme a Climatempo a média histórica para o mês é de 163 mm.

"A ocorrência foi identificada após o elevado volume de chuvas na região com ocorrências de mais de 170 milímetros de precipitação em apenas 24 horas, o que levou a companhia a intensificar as inspeções e o monitoramento da estrutura", afirmou a Corsan.

"Na tarde desta quarta-feira (23), a Defesa Civil do Estado foi informada pela Corsan sobre um possível rompimento da barragem Arroio São Luiz, localizada no município de São Marcos, após identificação de danos na estrutura da barragem. A evacuação preventiva de cerca de 60 edificações nas áreas potencialmente atingidas já foi iniciada, incluindo uma escola.

A Defesa Civil RS, através da 9ª Coordenadoria Regional, acompanha a situação no local, prestando apoio às equipes municipais, Corsan e demais forças de resposta. Um alerta Cell Broadcast foi enviado para a região às 15h53, orientando a população a se preparar para uma evacuação.

As equipes técnicas da Corsan identificaram trincas com vazamentos em partes da estrutura da barragem nesta quarta-feira. A companhia acionou o Plano de Ação de Emergências (PAE), dando início aos protocolos de retirada preventiva de pessoas para áreas seguras.

Profissionais técnicos da Corsan seguem com o monitoramento contínuo das condições da barragem. O Gabinete Integrado de Gerenciamento de Desastres (GIGED) instalou no município um Gabinete Local de Incidente."

"Monitoramento reforçado permite à Corsan identificar alteração e agir preventivamente na Barragem Arroio São Luiz

Alerta está restrito aos imóveis próximos à estrutura e às margens do Rio Jaguari; demais áreas de São Marcos não estão sob risco

As fortes chuvas dos últimos dias mobilizaram as equipes da Corsan responsáveis pelo monitoramento e vistoria das barragens. Em São Marcos, esse trabalho identificou trinca com vazamento na estrutura do vertedouro e em partes do contraforte da Barragem Arroio São Luiz. O alerta está restrito aos imóveis com essas duas condições combinadas - localizados próximos à estrutura e às margens do Rio Jaguari. As demais áreas da cidade não estão sob risco.

A região registrou mais de 170 milímetros de chuva em 24 horas. Assim que a alteração foi constatada, a Corsan acionou o Plano de Ação de Emergência (PAE), comunicou os órgãos competentes e intensificou o acompanhamento da estrutura.

Como medida preventiva, aproximadamente 170 pessoas que vivem na área de alerta estão sendo retiradas temporariamente. As famílias estão sendo deslocadas para locais seguros até a conclusão da avaliação técnica já contratada pela Companhia. O laudo dos especialistas permitirá dimensionar a situação e indicar as condições para o retorno aos imóveis.

Desde os eventos climáticos extremos de 2024, a Corsan reforçou seus protocolos de segurança, monitoramento e vistoria das estruturas no Rio Grande do Sul. O trabalho amplia a capacidade de identificar alterações e adotar rapidamente as medidas previstas para proteção da população.

Equipes técnicas permanecem no local acompanhando as condições da Barragem Arroio São Luiz. A Corsan manterá a população e os órgãos competentes informados conforme o avanço das avaliações."

articles.title: Netinho revela diagnóstico de câncer e anuncia pausa nos shows | G1
articles.standfirst: Cantor afirmou que tem câncer na amígdala e que fará uma cirurgia; ele deve ficar cerca de 30 dias afastado dos palcos
articles.summary: Cantor afirmou que tem câncer na amígdala e que fará uma cirurgia; ele deve ficar cerca de 30 dias afastado dos palcos
articles.body:
Cantor revelado como vocalista do grupo Negritude Junior, Netinho de Paula dá ótimos depoimentos na série — Foto: Reprodução / Vídeo

Netinho de Paula, de 56 anos, revelou que foi diagnosticado com câncer e anunciou uma pausa na agenda de shows para fazer uma cirurgia. Em um vídeo publicado em seu perfil no Instagram, o cantor afirmou que está tranquilo e disse que ficará cerca de 30 dias afastado dos palcos.

“Claro que não é normal você receber uma informação que você está com câncer. Isso não é uma coisa que é normal. Mas esse câncer é um câncer fraquinho", afirmou.

Netinho disse que decidiu falar sobre o diagnóstico depois que informações sobre sua doença foram publicadas na imprensa. Segundo o cantor, ele preferia não comentar o assunto anteriormente.

“É por isso que eu não quis sair falando para não estragar o sonho nem a alegria de ninguém. Mas hoje vazou na imprensa, então eu sou obrigado a comentar”, disse.

Na publicação, Netinho afirmou que vai suspender a agenda de shows no próximo mês para realizar o procedimento.

“Estou muito tranquilo, vou suspender minha agenda de shows no próximo mês, vou ter que ficar longe de vocês, vou sentir falta disso. Vai ser durante só 30 dias, mas eu vou fazer a cirurgia”, afirmou.

O cantor não informou, na fala, detalhes sobre o tipo específico de câncer, o estágio da doença ou o procedimento que será realizado. Ele também não deu outras informações sobre o tratamento.

Netinho disse que espera voltar aos palcos até o fim do ano. Durante o relato, mencionou um possível retorno a Manaus.

“E eu acho que até o final do ano eu já estou aqui de novo em Manaus fazendo pagode aqui para vocês. Eu estou aqui, vai dar tudo certo”, afirmou.

Ao final do vídeo, o cantor reforçou uma mensagem de tranquilidade para os fãs.

“É isso que o Brasil merece, alegria, nada de tristeza. Vai dar tudo certo.”

Artistas e amigos de Netinho de Paula deixaram mensagens de apoio ao cantor. Entre eles estão Belo, Tiaguinho e outros nomes ligados ao pagode, que desejaram força ao artista neste momento.

Netinho também disputa uma vaga de deputado federal por São Paulo nas eleições deste ano. Esta não é a primeira vez que o cantor entra na disputa eleitoral: ele já foi eleito vereador de São Paulo em 2008 e 2012. Também concorreu ao Senado em 2010 e à Câmara dos Deputados em 2014, mas não foi eleito.

articles.title: Muslims protest planned demolition of ‘600-year-old’ mosque in India
articles.summary: Hundreds of Muslims have gathered in the Indian city of Ujjain to protest the partial demolition of a historic mosque.
articles.body:
Muslims protest planned demolition of ‘600-year-old’ mosque in India

Hundreds of Muslims have gathered in the Indian city of Ujjain to protest the partial demolition of a mosque they say is more than 600 years old. The BJP-led state government says the action is needed to widen roads ahead of the 2028 Hindu pilgrimage, which is expected to draw large crowds.

articles.title: Mega-Sena: Duas apostas de Goiás levam juntas mais de R$ 145 mil | G1
articles.standfirst: As apostas foram realizadas nos municípios de Luziânia, no Entorno do Distrito Federal, e de São Luís de Montes Belos, no oeste de Goiás.
articles.summary: As apostas foram realizadas nos municípios de Luziânia, no Entorno do Distrito Federal, e de São Luís de Montes Belos, no oeste de Goiás.
articles.body:
Duas apostas feitas em Goiás acertaram cinco números da Mega-Sena e levaram juntas o valor de R$ 146.222,70. As apostas foram realizadas nos municípios de Luziânia , no Entorno do Distrito Federal, e de São Luís de Montes Belos , no oeste de Goiás.

Os números sorteados neste sábado (26) foram 05 - 35 - 36 - 41 - 43 - 48. Nenhum apostador acertou os seis números.

A aposta feita em Luziânia foi na modalidade bolão com cinco cotas, enquanto a aposta feita em São Luis de Montes, na modalidade simples. Cada aposta levou o prêmio no valor de R$ 73.111,35.

Outras 90 apostas em Goiás acertaram quatro números e levaram juntas o valor de R$ 150.800,03. Os prêmios para as apostas que acertaram quatro número variam entre R$1.322,81 e R$ 7.936,86.

Apostas em Luziânia e em São Luís de Montes Belos acertam cinco números e levam juntas mais de R$ 145 mil — Foto: Marcelo Camargo/Agência Brasil

Para ganhar na Mega-Sena, é preciso acertar, no mínimo, quatro números sorteados. Quem acerta seis números pode ganhar milhões de reais, marcando até 20 números disponíveis no volante, sendo o mínimo seis dígitos.

Há como deixar que sistema escolha os números, na modalidade Surpresinha e, também, como concorrer com a mesma aposta por até 12 sorteios consecutivos, na modalidade Teimosinha.

A aposta com o número mínimo de seis número custa R$ 5,00. O valor aumenta se tiver mais números marcados, porém aumentam as chances de faturar o prêmio.

articles.title: Bombeiros do AC encerram buscas por criança que desapareceu no AM | G1
articles.standfirst: Criança desapareceu no domingo (20), na Comunidade Descanso, próxima à cidade acreana de Sena Madureira. Equipe encerrou as buscas sem sucesso nesse sábado (26).
articles.summary: Criança desapareceu no domingo (20), na Comunidade Descanso, próxima à cidade acreana de Sena Madureira. Equipe encerrou as buscas sem sucesso nesse sábado (26).
articles.body:
As buscas por um menino de 2 anos que desapareceu na Comunidade Descanso, no Amazonas, foram encerradas nesse sábado (27). De acordo com o Corpo de Bombeiros do Acre, a criança não foi localizada após seis dias de procura na região.

Ao todo, cinco militares participaram da operação . Três deles foram enviados na última segunda-feira (21) e, posteriormente, mais dois mergulhadores que saíram de Rio Branco reforçaram a equipe.

👉Contexto: O menino desapareceu por volta das 16h do último domingo (20). A Comunidade Descanso fica em território amazonense, em uma área próxima a Sena Madureira , no interior do Acre. A família começou a procurar a criança com ajuda de moradores logo após perceber o desaparecimento. Ele foi visto caminhando por uma das ruas do local antes de desaparecer.

Conforme o Corpo de Bombeiros, moradores relataram ter encontrado pegadas próximas à margem do rio, o que levou os militares a concentrar a procura na área subaquática. A operação também contou com buscas superficiais na região.

Após a etapa subaquática, feita por mergulhadores, a equipe iniciou também as buscas superficiais na região.

Bombeiros do Acre fazem buscas por menino de 2 anos que desapareceu na Comunidade Descanso, no Amazonas — Foto: Corpo de Bombeiros

Além disso, assim que a criança desapareceu, a família relatou dificuldades para conseguir apoio especializado no estado amazonense.

Como a comunidade pertence territorialmente ao Amazonas, os familiares foram orientados inicialmente a buscar auxílio junto às equipes do estado , em razão de questões administrativas e de competência territorial.

Menino de 2 anos desapareceu na comunidade Descanso, no Amazonas, próximo a Sena Madureira — Foto: Reprodução

Segundo o soldado do Corpo de Bombeiros do Acre Kennedy Emanuel Sampaio da Silva, como a comunidade pertence ao Amazonas, existe um protocolo para a atuação dos bombeiros do Acre fora da área de jurisdição do estado.

Ainda conforme ele, como a família não obteve retorno das autoridades amazonenses, os bombeiros acreanos foram autorizados a se deslocar para a comunidade e ajudar nas buscas.

''O que existe é que por ser essa uma localidade de outra jurisdição (Estado) e aí existe um protocolo. Mas, fomos autorizados e a guarnição já se deslocou para o local'', explicou.

articles.title: Mega-Sena: aposta do interior de SP quase leva os R$ 45 milhões | G1
articles.standfirst: Jogo simples foi feito na Lotérica Pé Quente, em Mococa (SP); prêmio principal acumulou e subiu para R$ 52 milhões.
articles.summary: Jogo simples foi feito na Lotérica Pé Quente, em Mococa (SP); prêmio principal acumulou e subiu para R$ 52 milhões.
articles.body:
Bilhetes da Mega-Sena, em imagem de arquivo — Foto: Marcelo Brandt/G1

Uma aposta de Mococa (SP) acertou cinco das seis dezenas da Mega-Sena e ficou a um número de levar o prêmio de R$ 45 milhões , no sorteio deste domingo (27). O jogo faturou R$ 73.111,35.

A aposta simples, com seis números, foi feita na Lotérica Pé Quente, em Mococa. Como ninguém acertou as seis dezenas, o prêmio principal acumulou e subiu para R$ 52 milhões.

Os números sorteados no Concurso 3063 foram 05, 35, 36, 41, 43 e 48.

Mega-Sena, concurso 3.063: confira os números sorteados — Foto: Reprodução/Youtube Caixa

A aposta mínima custa R$ 6 e pode ser realizada também pela internet, até as 20h – saiba como fazer a sua aposta online.

Os jogos podem ser realizados até as 20h (horário de Brasília) em qualquer lotérica do país ou por meio do site e aplicativo Loterias Caixa, disponíveis em smartphones, computadores e outros dispositivos.

Já os bolões digitais poderão ser comprados até as 20h30, exclusivamente pelo portal Loterias Online e pelo aplicativo.

O pagamento da aposta online pode ser realizado via PIX, cartão de crédito ou pelo internet banking, para correntistas da Caixa. É preciso ter 18 anos ou mais para participar.

A Mega tem três sorteios semanais: às terças, quintas e domingos.

A probabilidade de vencer em cada concurso varia de acordo com o número de dezenas jogadas e o tipo de aposta realizada. Para um jogo simples, com apenas seis dezenas, que custa R$ 6, a probabilidade de ganhar o prêmio milionário é de 1 em 50.063.860, segundo a Caixa.

Já para uma aposta com 20 dezenas (limite máximo), com o preço de R$ 232.560,00, a probabilidade de acertar o prêmio é de 1 em 1.292, ainda de acordo com a instituição.

articles.title: Finding Desert Angels: Searching for the missing at the US-Mexico border
articles.summary: An ageing trailblazer of search and rescue risks his life to find a woman’s missing son in the US-Mexico borderlands.
articles.body:
Search-and-rescue pioneer Rafael Larraenza runs a harrowing, high-stakes DIY rescue operation for those who have gone missing after crossing the United States-Mexico border. For 25 years, Larraenza has been the man people call when no one else has the will, instincts or know-how to find their loved ones.

Now, facing physical decline and limited resources, Larraenza races against time to help a mother find her missing son, knowing that every minute can mean the difference between life and death. Desert Angel follows his dangerous journey through the deadly landscapes few ever see and some never escape.

Finding Desert Angels is a documentary film by Vincent DeLuca.

articles.title: Granizo em Santiago, no RS: Bombeiros distribuem 18 mil metros de lona | G1
articles.standfirst: Santiago, município de 48 mil habitantes na região central, teve mais de 4 mil pessoas afetadas em 1 mil moradias, conforme dados da Defesa Civil.
articles.summary: A chuva de granizo em Santiago RS afetou 4 mil pessoas e danificou mil casas, mobilizando a Defesa Civil na distribuição emergencial de lonas aos moradores.
articles.body:
O ginásio Aureliano de Figueiredo Pinto, em Santiago , na região central do RS, virou ponto de abrigo e distribuição de lona aos moradores do município atingido por forte chuva de granizo.

O Corpo de Bombeiros, Exército, Defesa Civil e outras autoridades já distribuíram, neste domingo (27), mais de 12 mil metros de lona a moradores da cidade. Os bombeiros também alertam que ainda não é momento para consertos, apenas para proteger a parte superior das moradias.

Em Santiago, moradores registraram a queda de pedras de gelo de grandes proporções, algumas com tamanho semelhante ao da palma da mão — foram 4 mil pessoas afetadas e ao menos 1 mil casas atingidas, segundo a Defesa Civil.

O temporal também afetou outras regiões do estado e atingiu, segundo a Defesa Civil, 6.347 pessoas.

Em Alegrete, na fronteira oeste do RS, pelo menos 300 casas foram atingidas pela chuva de granizo, e 2 mil pessoas, afetadas. O Instituto Federal Farroupilha, no município, suspendeu as aulas por tempo indeterminado depois da tempestade causar "danos significativos nas instalações do Campus". Não há registro de feridos.

Um grupo de caçadores de tempestades registrou uma supercélula em Alegrete , na tarde deste sábado (26). A formação foi filmada por volta das 18h50, durante a passagem de uma sequência de temporais pelo estado ( veja vídeo acima ).

🔎Os chamados caçadores de tempestades são pesquisadores aficionados por meteorologia e fenômenos atmosféricos que acompanham eventos de tempo severo para registrar e estudar essas formações.

Em alguns pontos da cidade, o volume de granizo foi tão grande que o chão ficou praticamente branco , como se estivesse coberto por uma camada de gelo.

Forte chuva de granizo em Santiago, no RS — Foto: Imagens cedidas/ Bibiana Thones

Balanço da Defesa Civil divulgado na manhã deste domingo (27):

6.347 pessoas afetadas (4 mil pessoas em Santiago; 2 mil pessoas em Alegrete)

Nenhum óbito confirmado, em investigação ou desaparecido

1.314 casas danificadas (1 mil casas em Santiago; 300 casas em Alegrete)

A instabilidade começou a avançar sobre a Fronteira Oeste do Rio Grande do Sul na tarde deste sábado.

Em Barra do Quaraí , houve registro de chuva com granizo . Já em Uruguaiana , um temporal chegou à região no início da noite.

Os fenômenos ocorrem em meio aos alertas emitidos pelo Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia (Inmet), pela Climatempo e pela Defesa Civil Estadual, que já apontavam risco de instabilidade entre esta sexta-feira (25) e a próxima segunda-feira (28) .

De acordo com os avisos meteorológicos, a mudança no tempo está associada à atuação de uma área de baixa pressão localizada entre o norte da Argentina e o Paraguai . Esse sistema favorece o transporte de ar quente e úmido em direção ao Rio Grande do Sul, criando condições para a formação de temporais.

Chegada de tempestade em Uruguaiana nesse sábado (26) — Foto: Pablo Gimenes/ RBS TV

No domingo (27) , a instabilidade ganha abrangência. A Defesa Civil alerta para ventos que podem superar 90 km/h e granizo grande na Campanha, Oeste, Missões, Noroeste, Norte e Centro. O calor segue intenso no Norte e Noroeste, alcançando 35 graus em Horizontina. No extremo sul, o clima é mais ameno, com mínima de 12 graus no Chuí.

A segunda-feira (28) mantém o tempo instável devido à organização de um novo sistema frontal. A Defesa Civil alerta que os acumulados totais de chuva entre sábado e segunda-feira podem passar de 200 milímetros na Campanha e no Oeste do estado. Apenas em 24 horas, os volumes podem superar 170 milímetros nestas regiões.

articles.title: Motoboy morre em acidente e motorista de carro é preso em João Pessoa | G1
articles.standfirst: Homem de 40 anos morreu após colisão de moto que pilotava com carro no cruzamento entre as Avenidas Beira Rio e Clemente Rosas, no bairro da Torre, na madrugada deste domingo (27).
articles.summary: Motoboy morre em João Pessoa após colisão no bairro da Torre; motorista foi autuado por homicídio culposo, na madrugada deste domingo (27).
articles.body:
Sirene Polícia Militar — Foto: Reprodução Google

Um motoboy, de 40 anos, morreu após a moto em que pilotava colidir com um carro no cruzamento entre as Avenidas Beira Rio e Clemente Rosas, no bairro da Torre, na madrugada deste domingo (27). O homem foi identificado como sendo Cleiton da Conceição e o motorista do carro foi preso em flagrante.

Devido ao impacto da colisão entre os veículos, o homem foi arremessado da moto a alguns metros e teve a perna esquerda decepada. O carro seguiu arrastando a moto por cerca de 100 metros de onde aconteceu a colisão.

O homem que pilotava o carro tem 39 anos e foi autuado por crime de trânsito com homicídio culposo. Ele ainda vai passar por audiência de custódia.

articles.title: Ônibus clandestino é apreendido após transportar passageiros sentados sobre caixas de cigarros ilegais no Paraná | G1
articles.standfirst: Policiais também encontraram cerca de 800 ampolas de emagrecedores contrabandeadas. Veículo tinha destino a duas cidades de Santa Catarina.
articles.summary: Policiais também encontraram cerca de 800 ampolas de emagrecedores contrabandeadas. Veículo tinha destino a duas cidades de Santa Catarina.
articles.body:
Passageiros estavam sentados sobre as caixas — Foto: Receita Federal

Cerca de 500 caixas de cigarro foram apreendidas em um ônibus clandestino em Foz do Iguaçu , no Oeste do Paraná, na noite de sábado (26).

Segundo a Receita Federal, os passageiros viajavam sentados sobre as caixas que escondiam os produtos ilegais, sem saber o que havia dentro delas .

Os cigarros também estavam armazenados na parte do bagageiro. Além disso, os policiais encontraram cerca de 800 ampolas de emagrecedores contrabandeadas no veículo.

O ônibus tinha destino as cidades de Criciúma e Tubarão, em Santa Catarina, e levava 22 passageiros sem ter a autorização da Agência Nacional de Transportes Terrestres (ANTT) para realizar o serviço.

Os dois motoristas, pai e filho, foram presos em flagrante pelos crimes de contrabando e descaminho. Eles foram levados à Delegacia de Foz do Iguaçu.

O ônibus foi lacrado e recolhido ao pátio da Receita Federal.

articles.title: Rússia ataca maior operadora de telefonia móvel da Ucrânia e atinge data centers | G1
articles.standfirst: Ataque ocorre em meio à intensificação dos bombardeios russos contra a infraestrutura de telecomunicações e data centers da Ucrânia; não houve vítimas na sede da operadora.
articles.summary: Ataque ocorre em meio à intensificação dos bombardeios russos contra a infraestrutura de telecomunicações e data centers da Ucrânia; não houve vítimas na sede da operadora.
articles.body:
Fumaça sobe sobre a sede da operadora Kyivstar, em Kiev, na Ucrânia — Foto: Reuters

A Rússia atacou neste domingo (27) a sede da Kyivstar, maior operadora de telefonia móvel da Ucrânia, informou a empresa à mídia local.

O ataque ocorreu enquanto Moscou mantinha bombardeios contra data centers e infraestrutura de comunicações do país.

A Kyivstar informou à agência de notícias Interfax Ucrânia que sua sede em Kiev foi atingida, mas não houve vítimas.

O Ministério da Defesa da Rússia também informou neste domingo que atingiu um data center da Vodafone Ucrânia, segunda maior operadora de telefonia celular do país.

A Vodafone Ucrânia não respondeu a um pedido de comentário.

O presidente ucraniano, Volodymyr Zelenskiy, afirmou que a Rússia atacou duas vezes um data center em Kiev na manhã deste domingo, ferindo duas crianças e um adulto.

Moscou também atingiu, na semana passada, data centers de provedores de internet ucranianos, provocando interrupções no serviço para cerca de 100 mil residências em Kiev e arredores, de acordo com o Ministério Digital da Ucrânia.

"A Rússia tem como alvo os principais data centers ucranianos, buscando interromper o fluxo de informações. Alertas rápidos sobre ameaças de mísseis e drones são essenciais -- eles salvam vidas", escreveu o ministro das Relações Exteriores da Ucrânia, Andrii Sybiha, no X na quarta-feira (23).

articles.title: Justiça determina que Prefeitura de Passos seja indenizada em R$ 136 mil por irregularidades em aluguel de trator  | G1
articles.standfirst: MPMG obteve condenação de ex-agentes públicos e empresa. Caso aconteceu em 2009.
articles.summary: MPMG obteve condenação de ex-agentes públicos e empresa. Caso aconteceu em 2009.
articles.body:
Prefeitura de Passos — Foto: Reprodução EPTV

A Justiça condenou ex-agentes públicos, particulares e uma empresa a ressarcirem R$ 136 mil ao município de Passos (MG), por prejuízos decorrentes de irregularidades na execução de um contrato de aluguel de trator para a prestação de serviços no aterro municipal.

O processo teve origem em investigação conduzida pelo MPMG para apurar possíveis irregularidades na execução de contrato decorrente de procedimento licitatório realizado pelo município em 2009 para a utilização do equipamento.

Após a análise das provas, o Judiciário concluiu que houve pagamento por horas a mais do que o necessário para a execução dos serviços, gerando dano aos cofres públicos.

De acordo com a sentença, a contratação previa número de horas de operação significativamente acima da demanda técnica apurada para o tratamento dos resíduos sólidos produzidos pelo município.

A Justiça considerou ainda que o controle dos serviços executados foi realizado de forma inadequada, sem mecanismos considerados mais seguros para aferição das horas trabalhadas.

A decisão aponta que as irregularidades resultaram em pagamentos indevidos e determinou o ressarcimento integral do valor correspondente ao prejuízo que foi identificado.

Embora as sanções previstas na antiga Lei de Improbidade Administrativa tenham sido consideradas prescritas ao longo da tramitação, permaneceu em julgamento o pedido de ressarcimento ao erário, que foi acolhido parcialmente pela Justiça.

A condenação foi imposta de forma solidária aos responsáveis reconhecidos na ação, o que significa que todos respondem conjuntamente pela devolução dos recursos ao erário municipal.

A identidade dos ex-agentes e da empresa não foi divulgada, o que impossibilitou o g1 de procurar as suas defesas.

articles.title: ‘Um professor’, diz primo ao relembrar que Rick o ajudaria com música | G1
articles.standfirst: Manoel contou que Rick sempre foi uma referência para ele e que ficou feliz com a possibilidade de desenvolver um trabalho musical juntos.
articles.summary: Manoel contou que Rick sempre foi uma referência para ele e que ficou feliz com a possibilidade de desenvolver um trabalho musical juntos.
articles.body:
O primo de Rick, da dupla com Renner, Manoel Filho, contou ao g1 , neste domingo (27), que se emociona ao falar do artista, que foi um “professor” na música. Manoel, conhecido artisticamente como Rafael, forma dupla com Thiago Mendonça e contou que Rick ajudaria os dois na produção de um videoclipe.

📱 Clique aqui para seguir o canal do g1 TO no WhatsApp

O cantor foi enterrado em Sorocaba (SP) no dia 24, no Cemitério Pax , na zona leste da cidade. Rick, o empresário Bruno Avelar, o videomaker Paulo Soares, o piloto Antônio Roberto Nóbrega de Araújo e o copiloto Leopoldo Barros Teixeira morreram na queda da aeronave em Santa Catarina, no dia 21.

Manoel contou que Rick sempre foi uma referência para ele e que ficou feliz com a possibilidade de desenvolver um trabalho musical juntos.

“Foi um grande professor. A gente sempre estava junto. Fiquei muito feliz no dia em que ele falou que ia mandar o playback da música e colocar a voz dele. Ele gostou bastante da dupla e aprovou o trabalho. ‘Está de parabéns. Você sabe como eu sou. Eu vou colocar a voz. Não é porque você é meu primo, é porque eu senti que vocês têm talento. A dupla é muito boa’.”

Manoel Filho à direita, de boné amarelo, ao lado de Renner, e Rick na ponta esquerda — Foto: Reprodução/Arquivo pessoal de Manoel FIlho de Martins

Rick, de fato, colocou a voz na música “O Chorão”, que está disponível no YouTube.

“No derradeiro abraço, o meu corpo estremeceu / minha alma ficou louca quando a sua boca me disse adeus / Fiz tudo pra não chorar, mas chorei sem querer / com a sua falta sei que vou sofrer, um grande vazio em meu coração / Já nem sei mais o que faço sem ela agora / esse é o motivo em que o homem chora, chorei e choro minha solidão”, narra a canção.

Antes da confirmação da morte, Manoel disse que aguardava a ligação do primo para definir as datas e o formato das gravações do videoclipe.

Batizado como Geraldo Antônio de Carvalho, o cantor Rick nasceu em Monte do Carmo, em 5 de dezembro de 1966, quando o Tocantins ainda era território goiano. Ele era casado com Geralda Helena de Carvalho havia mais de 40 anos. O casal teve dois filhos, Mônica e Victor Henrique, e quatro netos.

articles.title: Marra claims Scottish government 'hoarding power' in conference speech
articles.summary: The new Scottish Labour leader addressed the UK party conference in Liverpool a week after being elected.
articles.body:
The new leader of Scottish Labour has claimed the Scottish government has "hoarded money and control" at Holyrood and called for the decentralisation of powers to local regions.

Michael Marra called on the Scottish government to put "power and money" in the hands of "councils, colleges and industries" across the country to grow local economies.

In his inaugural speech to the UK Labour conference in Liverpool, Marra urged members not to mistake the SNP's "progressive posturing" for progressive politics.

He said it was his job to remind the people of Scotland what Labour stood for after the party's worst ever Holyrood election result in May.

Marra said: "Had our regions grown at the same pace as Manchester in the last decade, the Scottish economy would be £30bn larger.

"Too much power is centralised in Scotland. The Scottish government has hoarded money and control at the expense of Scotland's communities."

He attacked the SNP's record on education and child poverty, as well as the SNP administrations announcement that it would sack and re-hire 23,000 workers at Glasgow City Council.

Michael Marra announced as new Scottish Labour leader

Who is new Scottish Labour leader Michael Marra?

Marra used his conference speech to highlight Scotland's shipbuilding history as an example of failure in the government's skills policy.

He said Scotland has a reliance on foreign workers due to a lack of available, skilled Scottish equivalents.

"Shipbuilding – Scotland is famous for it," he said.

"We're world class at it. There should be a sense of national pride that the ships being built in Scotland are providing opportunity and security for Scottish workers.

"So, my message to Bute House is put control and money in the hands of the councils, colleges and industries who know what their local economies need better than any bureaucrat in Edinburgh."

Marra was speaking just a week after defeating Joe Fagan in a leadership election.

He replaced Anas Sarwar, who stood down to take up a a role in the House of Lords as part of Prime Minister Andy Burnham's government.

Marra said Burnham was the first person to phone him after his victory was announced.

He joked they may not agree on everything, including "dancing to The Smiths," but different "approaches and ideas" were welcome.

Scottish Labour's return of 17 MSPs saw them tied with Reform UK as the second-largest party in the Scottish Parliament.

He admitted the results of the May election "hurt" and the party had some "difficult truths to face up to".

Marra said he and Burnham did agree on the need for an "antidote" to a political "poison of hate, anger and fear".

He said the next UK election would be a straight fight between Labour and Reform.

Marra, who first joined Labour as a teenager , also spoke about his upbringing in Dundee in a family of ardent trade unionists.

He said he made his first leaflet run ahead of the 1987 general election at the age of eight, supporting Ernie Ross MP in Dundee West.

Marra said his grandmother Margaret, one of seven children, slept in a single room and was the only member of her family lucky enough to go to college while the others worked six days a week at the city's jute mills.

He said he was "forever grateful" for their sacrifice as the opportunity "changed her life" and her education changed Marra's, two generations later.

He said "not enough lives" in Scotland were being changed by education, and pledged to put Scottish education back among the world's best.

"It's no longer the SNP's priority, if it ever was," he said.

"I will make Scottish education the best in the world again. Not just steady, not just average, the best in the world again."

articles.title: First-ever images reveal mysterious remains of town swallowed by sea 700 years ago
articles.summary: Divers captured the first known images of Shipden, a medieval village lost to the North Sea for some 700 years. The pictures reveal massive flint structures.
articles.body: Divers recently captured the first-known images of mysterious underwater structures believed to be remnants of a village swallowed by the sea some 700 years ago. The images and video were recently taken off the coast of Norfolk in the United Kingdom, as news agency Jam Press reported. The remains are believed to be the lost town of Shipden, a medieval settlement that was eventually consumed by the North Sea in the 14th century. MYSTERIOUS SETTLEMENT DISCOVERED AFTER RESIDENTS SEEMINGLY PACKED UP AND VANISHED At the site, divers photographed and mapped 25 man-made features. Pictures show massive, marine-covered stone structures jutting from the sandy seabed as divers explored the centuries-old site. Volunteer divers from the East Anglian branch of the British Sub-Aqua Club (BSAC) helped survey and map the underwater site as part of the Alfred Savin Project's investigation. Despite the North Sea's reputation for rough and dangerous conditions, the water was unusually still during the summer dives — which helped the team photograph and map features on the seabed. FAINT SIGNAL LEADS TREASURE HUNTERS TO MASSIVE DISCOVERY AT LEGENDARY 400-YEAR-OLD WRECK The divers found structures made of flint — a popular building material in medieval Norfolk — as well as other pieces of cut stone and the remains of stone foundation structures known as caissons. The caissons may have been part of a 14th-century attempt to hold back the sea, but researchers have yet to determine their exact purpose. Some structures remain eight to 10 layers of stone high despite spending centuries underwater. The effort marks the first time the features are believed to have been photographed. UNDERWATER ROBOTICS EXPERT REVEALS 'SHIPWRECK CITY' HIDING BENEATH MAJOR URBAN LAKE Once a thriving village, Shipden was home to a modest population in the High Middle Ages. The Domesday Book — the survey that recorded land and populations across England following the Norman Conquest — noted that Shipden had just 117 residents in 1086. The town also boasted three acres of meadow, a harbor, two churches and "woodland capable of supporting 36 pigs," Jam Press noted. By the 14th century, its name gradually disappeared from records and the area became known as Cromer. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER Historical records confirm that a church was lost to the sea, but divers have yet to find any remains that can be definitively identified as the building. Legend holds that the tower of St. Peter's Church survived beneath the waves on a formation known as Church Rock. "For the present, we’re putting forward ideas rather than conclusions." Lead diver Nick Schiller told Jam Press the team initially set out to search for additional remains of the Victoria, a vessel that wrecked on Church Rock in 1888. "However, it’s been a bonus to help the Cromer team to take some steps forward in understanding the town of Shipden and the port of Cromer," said Schiller. CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS He said the findings suggest that Church Rock, long believed to be connected to the lost church, may instead be the remains of medieval sea defenses. For now, the location of the church remains a mystery. "Those of us brought up in Cromer have always known the story of Church Rock, so it’s a big step to saying the legend may be incorrect," Stibbons told Jam Press. articles.title: Israel’s Smotrich calls for ‘war’ in West Bank: Rhetoric or real threat?
articles.summary: Smotrich’s words should not be dismissed as mere election rhetoric, human rights experts and analysts warn.
articles.body:
Israel’s far-right Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich has called for a full-scale war in the occupied West Bank, urging the military to use the tactics employed in Gaza, which has been devastated by the ongoing genocide.

Smotrich, known for his inflammatory, racist and dehumanising language against Palestinians, also called for the annexation of southern Lebanon and Gaza’s territories under Israeli control.

The minister told Ynet News in an interview published on Sunday that Israel should “go to war” in the occupied territory and repeat what it “did in Gaza”. His comments come about a month ahead of the general election, which has seen a surge in Israeli and settler violence in the occupied territories, as well as the demonisation of Palestinian citizens of Israel.

During the Ynet News interview, Smotrich said that Israel should “do there what we did in Gaza” in response to a question on how Israel should combat the increasing “security tensions” in the occupied West Bank.

So what did the minister – who has been sanctioned by a number of Western countries along with his Cabinet colleague Itamar Ben-Gvir – say, and should it be taken seriously or regarded as just election rhetoric?

What did Smotrich say about the occupied West Bank?

In his trademark incendiary style, Smotrich said he has “solutions” to the ongoing pogroms in the occupied West Bank. Since Israel launched its ongoing genocidal war in Gaza, it has stepped up its crackdown in the West Bank, arrested thousands—many of them without any formal charges—and looked the other way as settler pogroms continue in the West Bank.

“I think we need to go to war in Judea and Samaria, to do there what we did in Gaza, to dismantle the Palestinian Authority, which is a terror authority,” he told Ynet News, referring to the biblical name for the West Bank. The Palestinian Authority governs the West Bank following the Oslo Accords.

Israeli forces have “cleared out” Palestinian refugee camps in the West Bank and he added: “We need to tell the [Israeli military]: Just as you dismantled Hamas in Gaza, there won’t be terror infrastructure in Judea and Samaria. No terrorists, no weapons, no tunnels”.

That’s alarming rhetoric, warned Suhad Bishara, the legal director of Adalah – the Legal Center for Arab Minority Rights in Israel.

“Smotrich is not only proposing a ‘war’ on Palestinians in the West Bank, he is already waging one,” Bishara told Al Jazeera.

“The refugee camps he boasts of having ‘cleared out’ have been destroyed and their residents forcibly displaced.”

“His call to ‘do there what we did in Gaza,’ where Israel has carried out a genocidal campaign of mass killing, starvation and destruction, is a public declaration of intent to commit war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide against Palestinians in the West Bank,” she said.

Smotrich additionally pushed to annex the territory the Israeli military controls in Gaza, demarcated by the so-called “Yellow Line”, where the Israeli army withdrew to under the first phase of the Gaza “ceasefire”. Israeli military maps indicate the line extends 1.5km and 6.5km (0.9 to 4 miles) inside Gaza from its eastern boundary with Israel and covers roughly 58 percent of the enclave.

Since the “ceasefire” took effect, Israeli attacks have killed at least 1,408 Palestinians. At least 74,000 Palestinians have been killed by Israel since October 2023, according to the enclave’s health ministry, with much of the besieged territory reduced to rubble.

Legal scholars and campaigners have dubbed Israel’s military actions in Gaza a genocide. A UN commission of inquiry panel last September said that Israel committed genocide in Gaza.

What were Smotrich’s remarks about Lebanon?

The leader of the far-right Religious Zionism party also called for annexing southern Lebanon.

“I would very much like to annex at least up to the “Yellow Line” in Gaza and up to the Litani [River] in Lebanon,” said Smotrich.

He added that annexing parts of Gaza and Lebanon would make Israel’s enemies “pay a price” for the Hamas-led attack on October 7, 2023.

Israel continues to occupy southern Lebanon and Israeli shelling and demolitions have also continued there, despite a US-brokered “ceasefire” in June.

Smotrich’s call to annex the West Bank, parts of Gaza and southern Lebanon is a “declared plan to seize occupied land by force and make its theft permanent, which is absolutely prohibited under international law,” said Bishara.

Last week, Lebanon’s Prime Minister Nawaf Salam, speaking at the United Nations General Assembly in New York, demanded a complete withdrawal of Israeli forces from Lebanese territory up to its internationally recognised border.

Israeli attacks in southern Lebanon have killed at least 4,386 people and wounded 12,407 since March 2, when the current Hezbollah-Israel war started. Since then, Israeli forces have occupied up to 600sq km of Lebanese territory up to the Litani River.

How have Palestinian authorities responded?

The Palestinian Ministry of Foreign Affairs said the Israeli politician’s comments are an “explicit invitation to escalate the aggression and commit more crimes against our Palestinian people”.

They “reveal the truth of the Israeli plans aimed at implementing attempts at annexation and displacement”, the ministry said in a statement, adding that it would undermine the possibility of establishing an independent Palestinian state.

The threats are a translation of the policies pursued by the Israeli government “of killing, displacement, settlement, and land confiscation and an attempt to impose a new reality by force on the occupied Palestinian land”, it also said.

The ministry urged the international community to take action against Israel’s “aggression”.

The far-right leader has a long history of inflammatory statements about Palestinians, followed by policies and actions reflecting his hardline positions as a key member of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s far-right government since 2022.

He has previously called on Israel to annex more than 80 percent of the West Bank. Smotrich along with Netanyahu has publicly opposed the so-called two-state solution. Settlement expansion is the biggest hurdle in the realisation of a sovereign and independent Palestinian state living side by side with Israel.

In July, Smotrich said Israel has launched a “revolution in settlement” expansion , after the Israeli cabinet approved the establishment of 13 new illegal settlements in the central occupied West Bank. That followed June’s announcement of 2,162 new Jewish homes in a new illegal settlement near Jerusalem.

In campaigning for next month’s election, he has promised yet more expansions of Israeli settlements in the territory.

“Settler violence, carried out under army protection, is driving entire communities from their land and settlement expansion under his authority has reached unprecedented levels,” said Bishara.

In May, Smotrich said the ⁠⁠⁠⁠International Criminal ⁠⁠⁠⁠Court (ICC) had ⁠⁠⁠⁠requested a warrant for his arrest. The ICC’s accusations centre on the minister’s forced displacement orders for Palestinians, his support for moving Israeli settlers into occupied territory and his claim it may be “ justified and moral ” to starve Palestinians in Gaza.

Last September, before the “ceasefire” in Gaza, Smotrich said there was a “business plan” to turn the Strip into a “real estate bonanza”, stating that he had been discussing with the Trump administration how to share the proceeds.

In March, he also threatened to turn the southern suburbs of Lebanon’s capital into another Gaza Strip.

Smotrich’s words should not be dismissed as mere election rhetoric, warned Bishara.

“They are a warning and states must take concrete, immediate measures to halt the assault on Palestinians and the commission of egregious crimes against them,” she said.

Analysts agreed with the human rights lawyer’s assessment.

“[Smotrich’s comment is] very much a reflection of what he has been doing in the West Bank for the last four years and what he would like to continue to do if he stays in power,” Mairav Zonszein, an analyst on Israel-Palestine at the International Crisis Group, told Al Jazeera.

“Him and this government and the settler movement that he funds and resources … they are at war in the West Bank.”

She explained that Smotrich and his allies have used settlement expansion and settler violence not only to expand their control, but also to provoke a Palestinian response.

“And any response by Palestinians is met with even more ferocious force,” said Zonszein.

Smotrich is not just gearing up for next month’s election – he has a calculated vision of wanting to continue his expansionist policies, she said.

“It’s the government’s vision, and it’s what they’ve been doing, and this is what they will continue to do as long as they’re in power.”

Yossi Mekelberg, a senior fellow on Israel-Palestine at Chatham House, said that while Smotrich’s comments may be a part of his election campaign, “what is now rhetoric, tomorrow may be policy”.

“We are exactly a month from the election … If this is the tone … and this is what’s presented to the voters and if someone like him on the basis of this ideology will be elected again, he might find it as [an] endorsement of this kind of attitude,” Mekelberg told Al Jazeera.

articles.title: Orange Order march row goes to heart of ongoing divisions in Northern Ireland
articles.summary: The dispute over the controversial parade is a reminder that the peace process is not over.
articles.body:
History shows that when the politics of Northern Ireland are wrapped up in a street dispute, friction is seldom far away.

Bitter rows in the Stormont chamber between unionists and nationalists happen almost every week, but ground-level arguments are rare these days.

The Drumcree parade dispute in Portadown is a clash of political cultures.

The Orange Order is a Protestant pro-British organisation. The area where it wants to walk is largely Catholic, and predominantly inhabited by pro-Irish nationalists.

This dispute over a piece of road is not just a local problem. It has the potential to affect other parts of Northern Ireland and the power-sharing arrangements at Stormont.

"What happens at Drumcree never stays at Drumcree," was how one retired politician put it.

What is the Garvaghy Road dispute all about?

When the parade dispute first erupted into violence in the mid-1990s, the disorder spread to other places - and almost derailed the peace process.

But while it was never fully resolved, the dispute faded over the next 30 years. Its sudden re-emergence has caught most people by surprise, including many politicians.

What happened was that a legal case was brought to court over the dispute early this summer, re-opening the debate.

The two largest parties in Northern Ireland, Sinn Féin and the Democratic Unionist Party (DUP), have been on opposite sides of the argument.

Sinn Féin are firmly behind the residents. The DUP fully supports the Orange Order.

They may be partners in the devolved government at Stormont, but when it comes to Drumcree they could not be further apart.

As always in Northern Ireland, the historical context is important.

Although there has been an uneasy calm in Portadown over the parading issue in recent years, the Orange Order regards the march as unfinished business.

In 1998, it was banned from completing its Drumcree march - which includes the Garvaghy Road - and has been repeatedly refused permission to finish the route ever since.

It has applied and been turned down more than 1,000 times in the past three decades.

It says it is being denied a traditional walk which dates back to the early 1800s.

A Parades Commission was set up in the late 1990s to adjudicate on marching disputes and, until now, it has consistently ruled against the route.

The Orange Order's legal challenge to a ruling in June this year succeeded on procedural grounds.

The order subsequently re-applied for permission to carry out the parade, albeit a scaled-back version with only 35 participants rather than 400 - and was successful.

Nationalist residents on the Garvaghy Road were left shocked and angry.

For them, the parade is triumphalist and unwelcome in the area.

Rather than being about tradition, they see the parade as an act of supremacy and say it re-opens old community wounds.

During a last-minute legal battle over the march, a judge appealed for all sides of the dispute to find common ground and come to an agreement.

Nobody was surprised when that did not happen.

Feelings are running high on the issue on all sides, including among the political parties.

Relations in the power-sharing executive are now dangerously close to breaking point.

There is a Stormont election next year which means parties tend to dig in, rather than search for compromises.

The Drumcree dispute goes to the heart of the divisions which remain in Northern Ireland.

Events of recent days are a reminder that the peace process is not over, it is ongoing - and there is still work to be done on the ground and at Stormont.

images.caption: Hundreds of protesters blocked the parade route after it was given clearance for the first time in almost 30 years

articles.title: Yemen’s health system could collapse in some areas, minister warns
articles.summary: Yemen’s healthcare system may not be able to support the population as war strains resources, minister tells Al Jazeera.
articles.body:
Some areas in Yemen could suffer from a complete loss of health services if a decline in funding continues, Yemen’s Minister of Public Health and Population Qasim Buhaibeh has told Al Jazeera.

He said that the health sector may not be able to absorb additional waves of displacement from the ongoing war while a lack of resources has forced the closure of health facilities and caused shortages of medicines, supplies and fuel.

Buhaibeh added that emergency services, maternal and child healthcare, vaccination and nutrition services, as well as dialysis and cancer treatment, are all particularly threatened by the decline in funding.

He noted that health data updated through June 2026 indicates that 19.3 million people in Yemen require health assistance, while funding for the response has reached only 17 percent of the required amount.

Buhaibeh said that the proportion of health facilities operating at full capacity has likely dropped to less than 50 percent. The World Health Organization had cited 60 percent .

The minister cited figures indicating that 134,550 people have been displaced by the war between June and September 22, with most of them being in Taiz, Lahij and Aden. He said the influx of displaced people has placed additional pressure on health facilities that were already struggling with limited resources.

Buhaibeh said the reporting of health data from Houthi-controlled areas has been suspended for nearly a year, preventing authorities from forming a complete nationwide picture of the epidemiological situation.

Additionally, Buhaibeh warned that displacement, malnutrition and low vaccination coverage are coinciding with outbreaks of cholera, measles and polio.

He noted that more than 27,000 confirmed measles cases were recorded in 2025 and that around half of Yemen’s children under the age of five suffer from chronic malnutrition.

The International Organization for Migration (IOM) has found that nearly 130,000 people, or 30,000 households, have been displaced across seven governorates in Yemen since fighting escalated between the Iran-backed Houthis and the internationally recognised Yemeni government coalition forces in early September.

articles.title: New lithium mine in Cornwall 'set to create more than 100 jobs'
articles.summary: Officials say demand for lithium is expected to increase by 1,100% by 2035.
articles.body:
A new lithium mine is set to create more than 100 jobs under government plans, bosses say.

Geothermal Engineering Limited said it would invest about £43m in a lithium extraction facility in Cornwall, which it planned to bring into commercial production in 2029.

Officials said it was part of government plans to boost industrial resilience and help secure vital supply chains backing automotive, clean energy and advanced manufacturing sectors.

CEO Dr Ryan Law said the UK had an important opportunity to develop resources, technology and expertise for a domestic lithium supply, and they were "proud to be building that capability here in Cornwall, bringing jobs and new investment to the local area."

The government has taken action to unlock nearly £230m of private investment into two lithium projects in Cornwall and Teesside, the company said.

Lithium is needed for making batteries for electric vehicles.

The move came as demand for lithium was expected to increase by 1,100% by 2035 and would support hundreds of jobs and shore up Britain's supplies of lithium, it added.

Officials said the investment in Cornwall would create nearly 50 direct jobs and support about 80 more across the supply chain, after receiving an offer in principle worth nearly £10m through the Government's DRIVE35 Automotive Transformation Fund.

Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds said the most would help unlock the region's "industrial potential".

"Hot on the heels of over £1bn of automotive investment secured already this month, this latest win is a big step towards building our industrial resilience," he said.

Officials said £1bn of investment was announced this month from Bentley, McLaren and Nissan.

The facility is expected to produce around 1,500 tonnes of technical-grade lithium carbonate from geothermal brine underground each year – enough to power more than 180,000 typical EV car batteries.

Officials said the facility had the potential to scale to produce tens of thousands of tonnes in the future, and the lithium produced would give a huge boost to the UK's EV battery manufacturing, shoring up crucial supply chains and moving Britain forward in the transition towards net zero.

Julian Hetherington, automotive transformation and engagement director, APC and Zenzic, said extracting lithium in the UK diminished dependence on supply chains.

"In addition, the lithium extraction is expected to spark significant economic growth, especially in Cornwall where a vibrant materials cluster is developing at pace," Hetherington added.

articles.title: 4 killed, 4 wounded in mass shooting near capital of Caribbean luxury tourism destination
articles.summary: Four people were killed and four wounded in a shooting near Kingstown in St. Vincent and the Grenadines as police search for those responsible.
articles.body: A shooting near the capital of St. Vincent and the Grenadines left four people dead and four others wounded Friday night, prompting an intensified police response in the Caribbean island nation as authorities search for those responsible. Gunfire erupted shortly before 10:30 p.m. in the Green Hill community near Kingstown, according to Acting Commissioner of Police Trevor Bailey, who addressed the killings during a Saturday news conference. Officers responding to the scene found two bodies on a public road, while a woman was found dead inside a vehicle parked nearby, Bailey said. A fourth victim was discovered on an adjacent piece of land. All four appeared to have suffered gunshot wounds. GUNFIRE SHATTERS TORONTO LATIN STREET FESTIVAL, LEAVING AT LEAST 2 DEAD AND MULTIPLE WOUNDED Four additional people were taken to Milton Cato Memorial Hospital with gunshot injuries. Two were treated and released, while two remained hospitalized at the time of the police briefing. No arrests had been made, and police had not publicly identified a motive. Assistant Commissioner of Police Brenton Smith said investigators were working to identify whoever was responsible and cautioned against speculation while the investigation remained active. Police were also investigating a separate shooting in Ottley Hall early Saturday and had not determined whether the two incidents were connected. AT LEAST 3 DEAD, 23 WOUNDED IN SEPARATE MASS SHOOTINGS LESS THAN 15 MINUTES APART "That determination must be made by investigators based on the evidence and not on rumors or assumptions," Smith said. The killings come as authorities grapple with gun and gang violence across the small island nation. Smith said 37 murders have been recorded in St. Vincent and the Grenadines so far this year. Bailey acknowledged that police have seen instances of retaliatory violence involving rival groups but did not link the Green Hill killings to gang activity. Asked whether criminal groups could be connected to the latest violence, police said the investigation had not reached a point where they could make such a determination. Authorities said additional patrols, random searches and intelligence operations were underway in Kingstown and surrounding communities as police attempt to recover illegal firearms and prevent further violence. Local outlet iWitness News reported that the Green Hill attack was one of several shootings in recent years in which multiple people were killed, including a July shooting in Kingstown that left three people dead. The outlet reported the identities of Friday's four victims based on its own sources, though police had not officially released their names when the report was published. The violence occurred in a country heavily promoted for its secluded Caribbean setting and high-end tourism. St. Vincent and the Grenadines consists of 32 islands and cays and is promoted by the country's tourism authority as a destination for sailing, beaches, coral reefs and secluded getaways. Mustique, one of its inhabited islands, is known for private villas and celebrity visitors, while the broader archipelago is a major destination for yachts and sailing. articles.title: Guildford council's search starts for new theatre operator
articles.summary: Guildford Borough Council is appealing for expressions of interest to run the Electric Theatre.
articles.body:
Those interested in running a council-owned theatre, which closed after recording losses of £250,000, are being urged to submit an expression of interest.

Guildford Borough Council, which owns the Electric Theatre, says it wants to understand the level of interest in the community arts venue and identify future management options before a formal procurement process.

Vanessa King, the council's deputy leader, said: "We're keen to hear from the widest range of interested parties, from community-led and charitable organisations through to commercial and alternative-use operators."

Written expressions of interest and completed operator response forms must be submitted by midday on 30 October.

The Surrey council said it was also looking for views on how operators could provide local employment opportunities, affordable pricing, high-quality programming and a resilient business model.

The operators of the Electric Theatre in Guildford cancelled shows from April 2025 after recording the losses in 2023-24.

The theatre was leased out to ACM Commercial Ltd until it went into administration in May 2025, with the lease being surrendered to the council in August that year.

Julia McShane, leader of the council, said: "This has always been about working with our community to find the best way forward.

"The views shared have helped us reach this important stage and will continue to inform the decisions we make as we move ahead."

articles.title: In 2020, a New Jersey man lost his job and began mowing lawns for free; six years later, his volunteer network has grown to more than 2,000 people across all 50 US states
articles.summary: When Brian Schwartz lost his digital marketing job during the COVID-19 pandemic in the summer of 2020, he pulled out his lawnmower and began cutting grass
articles.body: When Brian Schwartz lost his digital marketing job during the COVID-19 pandemic in the summer of 2020, he pulled out his lawnmower and began cutting grass for elderly neighbors in Wayne, New Jersey. Six years later, that simple act has grown into a nationwide volunteer movement operating in all 50 U.S. states. According to figures published by the initiative's official website, I Want To Mow Your Lawn, the nonprofit network now has more than 2,000 volunteers across the country. Together, they provide free lawn mowing, leaf raking and snow removal for senior citizens, military veterans, people with disabilities and others in need. The organization uses a digital platform to connect local people who have outdoor power equipment with residents who need physical or financial help caring for their properties.Turning redundancy into community serviceSchwartz was working in digital advertising when his firm closed during the pandemic in June 2020, leaving him without a job. He was dealing with isolation and uncertainty and wanted to find an outdoor activity that would keep him active while allowing him to follow social distancing rules. He decided to help older residents in his neighborhood who could not manage their yards during the lockdown. He created a website and offered free lawn mowing to people age 65 and older. The response came quickly. Schwartz soon received requests from people outside his immediate neighborhood. He used his own lawnmower and paid for the fuel himself. "I'd gone out to mow my lawn and it felt therapeutic, it was a good workout and helped me to clear my mind," Schwartz told The Washington Post. "So I thought, 'That's it, I'll give back by mowing lawns and doing yard work for people who are having trouble doing it on their own.'" His first request came from an elderly woman in Verona, New Jersey. Her son normally cared for her lawn but was too busy with work to mow it. Schwartz loaded his mower and edger into his Jeep and drove 30 miles to help her, according to The Washington Post. As more requests arrived, Schwartz used his background in web development and search engine optimization to build a dedicated online system. The site allowed people who needed help to request lawn visits and gave volunteers a way to sign up.Building a technology platform for volunteersThe platform helps connect volunteers with people who need yard work in their area. Volunteers can see available requests and decide when they want to help. The nonprofit also works to make the process safe for the people receiving help. Its website provides tools for coordinating volunteers and yard-care requests without requiring a long-term commitment. According to I Want To Mow Your Lawn, the effort grew from a small New Jersey project into a national nonprofit. Volunteers joined from across the country, helping older adults, veterans, people with disabilities and others who could not manage their yards themselves. The organization also attracted attention from the landscaping industry. Landscape Management reported on Schwartz's work and the growth of I Want To Mow Your Lawn. The publication has continued to cover the nonprofit as it expanded into a nationwide volunteer effort. The nonprofit has also expanded its work beyond summer lawn mowing. Volunteers can help with other outdoor tasks, including leaf removal and snow clearing, giving older residents help with jobs that can be difficult or unsafe to handle alone.Supporting elderly and veteran residentsFor many people who receive the free service, the help is about more than keeping their yards neat. It can also give them a chance to see and speak with someone when they may otherwise spend much of their time alone. I Want To Mow Your Lawn says it provides free lawn care to elderly people, military veterans, people with disabilities and others in need. The organization was created in 2020 and operates as a 501(c)(3) nonprofit. Schwartz has said that mowing his own lawn became a form of therapy after he lost his job. That experience led him to offer the same kind of help to people who were struggling to care for their homes. The organization's official website now says the network has reached all 50 states and has more than 2,000 volunteers. The group remains volunteer-run and focuses on connecting people who need temporary yard-care help with people willing to provide it. Schwartz continues to run the organization from New Jersey, helping oversee its technology, volunteer network and partnerships. What began with one unemployed man, one lawnmower and a desire to help his neighbors has grown into a national movement built around a simple idea, helping someone with a job as ordinary as cutting their grass can make a real difference.You use AI every day. articles.title: Social care reform could mean big risks and big rewards for Burnham
articles.summary: The state of the social care system in England is a topic that's made Andy Burnham angry for decades - but will his plans for reform work?
articles.body:
The state of the social care system in England is a topic that's made Andy Burnham angry for decades.

As Gordon Brown's health secretary he proposed a compulsory levy collected from people's estates – an idea the Conservatives dubbed the "death tax".

He repeatedly returned to the issue when making interventions as the Mayor of Greater Manchester, and in his first major interview as prime minister back in July , Burnham pledged to put "whatever political capital I have into fixing broken social care".

We now have the first outline about how he hopes to do that.

But there are a host of unanswered questions about how the government would fund and deliver what could be an eye-wateringly expensive and politically perilous idea.

The prime minister told the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg that he will go into the next election proposing a free-to-use, universally funded national care system.

Past governments have looked at how to reform social care and balked at the potential costs.

The Health Foundation has previously estimated that a free system could end up costing the taxpayer around £18bn a year.

Burnham denied that figure but conceded that tackling the issue could make him "unpopular" with some.

He stressed that the current system comes with hidden costs for individuals and the state, such as people losing their houses to pay for costs and spending time in A&E because their home care isn't adequate.

But it's difficult to deny that this idea would come with a staggering up front cost and one the prime minister would have to lay out a far more detailed funding plan for, if he went into an election with this as his flagship proposal.

The last prime minister to attempt a substantial overhaul of social care was Theresa May, whose 2017 plans unfurled when they were nicknamed the "dementia tax".

Burnham said the manifesto that Labour was elected on at the last general election would make it "hard" to achieve his goal.

That's a clear hint that he could well go into the next election pledging to increase tax in order to fund social care.

The manifesto that Burnham is currently bound by pledged not to hike income tax, VAT or National Insurance.

Other funding options are not being taken off the table, including a return to Burnham's old plan to make some people pay out of their inheritance.

He could also get some political cover, in the form of an ongoing review by the longtime policy guru Baroness Casey.

She's been heading a commission into adult social care since April last year and Burnham said her findings would influence what he proposes.

It's understood she's been asked to find a "sustainable" solution, and it would be within her remit to recommend tax changes and cuts to other areas of spending, to raise the money needed.

The prime minister wouldn't engage with the question of what areas he might cut but did promise more meat on the bones of his social care plans when he makes his speech to the Labour Party conference on Tuesday.

Andy Burnham wants to fix social care - what are the options?

Burnham proposes NHS-style social care system for England

NHS 'will collapse' without social care reform, PM tells BBC

Darren Jones, who was Sir Keir Starmer's chief secretary, and has assumed the mantle of an internal Burnham critic, warned against taxing, spending and borrowing, without making cuts.

He suggested that if Burnham wanted to prioritise social care, he may need to look at scrapping the triple lock for pensioners, which Labour's 2024 manifesto pledged to keep.

The Conservatives have already criticised the potential for increasing the tax burden and Reform have described Burnham's plan as another "death tax".

Some Labour MPs would undoubtedly be uncomfortable at the prospect of having to sell controversial decisions like tax rises or changes to the triple lock, on the doorstep at the next election.

But there's been a general trend in recent years among both the Conservative and Labour parties, of backbenchers grumbling about party leaders being unwilling – perhaps not brave enough – to make forthright political arguments.

Burnham hasn't yet revealed the finer details, but for now, at least, he's confident enough in his own ability to win the argument.

Those around the PM believe there are enormous plaudits to be won for whoever manages to adequately fix the system.

History would suggest, though, that prime ministers who fail to convince the public on social care reforms don't last long in the job.

It may be an issue he's talked about for years, but on social care, Andy Burnham is taking a big swing.

articles.title: For Libya, the Hormuz crisis can be a trap or an opportunity
articles.summary: Libyan hydrocarbons are increasingly sought after. To take full advantage, the country needs a new economic strategy.
articles.body:
Amid the worsening global energy crisis triggered by the US-Israel war on Iran, European countries, desperate for alternative energy supplies, trade routes and partnerships, have looked across the Mediterranean for solutions.

As a result, governments across North Africa have started to reassess their strategic value. Algeria is in an especially strong position as an established gas supplier, while Egypt can offer infrastructure, refining capacity and access through the Suez Canal.

Libya has also seen its strategic value increase. It has around 48 billion barrels of proven oil reserves, the largest in Africa , and produces 1.5 million barrels of oil per day. It also has substantial natural gas reserves.

Its oil reaches international markets through the Mediterranean, while the Greenstream gas pipeline connects its Mellitah complex directly to Europe.

Libya cannot replace the Gulf in terms of oil and gas exports, but it can become a major player in diversification efforts not just in Europe but elsewhere in the world. The challenge the country faces is how to take full advantage amid structural constraints and insecurity.

Libya is simultaneously a major energy exporter and an energy-insecure state. Although the country possesses vast oil and gas resources, Libyans experience regular electricity blackouts due to an inefficient domestic energy system.

More than 70 percent of Libyan gas production is consumed domestically, mostly for electricity generation. Production has struggled to meet both domestic needs and export commitments. Gas exports consequently fell year on year from around 200 billion cubic feet in 2019 to 35 billion in 2025, the lowest export levels in 22 years.

At the same time, the country is flaring at least 200 billion cubic feet of gas annually due to underdeveloped infrastructure. Gas that could generate electricity, support industry or increase exports is instead being wasted.

The International Monetary Fund has estimated Libya’s total energy subsidy burden at around $17bn, equivalent to roughly 35 percent of GDP – one of the largest in the world.

Much of these funds go into subsidising imported refined fuels, as domestic refining capacity is largely underdeveloped and cannot meet demand.

The domestic energy situation is compounded by political fragmentation, institutional disputes and periodic disruptions to production due to conflict.

Increasing exports without addressing these problems risks improving energy security abroad while neglecting it at home, and that is a recipe for more instability in an already fragile nation.

The global energy crisis triggered by the Iran war is surely a major opportunity for Libya to increase its revenues from hydrocarbons. But it also carries a risk.

As I pointed out during the 5th meeting of the Mediterranean Energy Experts Circle earlier this month, greater demand for Libyan oil and gas could reinforce the economic model the country has struggled to escape from for decades: producing hydrocarbons, exporting them, distributing the revenues and postponing structural reform.

This model does not allow Libya to capture the full economic potential of its resource wealth. It keeps the Libyan state stuck in the all too familiar “resource curse”, which promotes economic stagnation and inefficiency.

That is why when taking advantage of heightened demand for energy, it is crucial that Libya uses the proceeds to transform its energy system.

That means capturing flared gas, modernising electricity generation and transmission, expanding domestic refining where economically viable, reforming subsidies, investing seriously in renewable energy and participating in sustainable regional energy cooperation.

Libya’s National Sustainable Energy Strategy aims to have 22 percent of electricity generation from renewable sources by 2035, an ambitious target that requires major positive shifts in security and governance conditions. Increased revenue flows can help jump-start the process.

Another important consideration is how the country should approach heightened foreign interest. Libya’s first major oil and gas licensing round since 2007 was concluded in February, with the US’s Chevron, Italy’s Eni, QatarEnergy, Spain’s Repsol, Hungary’s MOL, Nigeria’s Aiteo, and Türkiye’s TPAO securing new licences.

Commercial and geopolitical interests are rarely completely separate in energy. For Libya, this creates bargaining power—if managed coherently by the Libyans. Rather than becoming an arena in which external actors compete for individual assets and relationships, Libya could use diversified partnerships to attract investment and technology while reducing dependence on any single partner.

From energy exporter to Mediterranean energy hub

The transformation Libya seeks should not be confined to its borders. Its strategic objective should be to become an integral player in a Mediterranean energy hub by expanding cooperation with neighbouring states and leveraging existing production capacities and infrastructure.

To Libya’s east, Egypt has a large electricity system and significant refining and processing capacity. To its west, Tunisia provides access towards the wider Maghreb and increasingly towards European markets. Libya sits between them with enormous hydrocarbon resources, considerable solar potential and existing energy connections with both neighbours.

Important steps have already been taken to deepen regional energy integration. In January, Egypt and Libya signed an energy cooperation agreement covering exploration and the development of crude-oil refining. The two countries are also discussing the construction of an 800km pipeline connecting Tobruk to Alexandria. The project is worth $1bn and would carry Libyan crude directly to Egyptian refineries.

Libya and Tunisia are also expanding cooperation. Earlier this month, the Libyan-Tunisian company Joint Oil opened an international licensing round covering around 3,000 square kilometres of shared offshore acreage and development of the cross-border Zarat oil and gas discovery. Formal awards are expected by the end of April 2027.

The risk here is that expanded cooperation could develop into dependence. How to avoid that is the lesson Libya can learn from the Strait of Hormuz crisis. The country still needs sufficient domestic electricity, refining and production capacity to protect itself. Regional integration should add alternatives rather than create new vulnerabilities: more markets, more electricity connections, more processing options and more export routes.

The objective should therefore be specialisation, connectivity and redundancy all achieved in the right sequence depending on needs and conditions.

The Iran war has given Libya something potentially more valuable than temporarily higher hydrocarbon prices: renewed strategic relevance. But greater strategic relevance does not automatically make the country a more reliable energy partner.

Converting the former into the latter requires a radically different approach not just to the domestic oil and gas industry, but also to overall economic development and regional geopolitics.

Libya must use this moment to pursue strategic redesign: to increase production while recovering wasted gas, improve electricity infrastructure, develop refining and renewables, strengthen regional connections and cooperation, and use competition among international partners to attract investment.

Libya already has the resources and the geography to become an even bigger player in the energy market. The question is whether it can build the rest.

The views expressed in this article are the author’s own and do not necessarily reflect Al Jazeera’s editorial stance.
